9
Two gliders are travelling towards each other on a horizontal air track. Glider P has mass 0.30 kg
and is moving with a constant speed of 1.2 m s–1. Glider Q has mass 0.60 kg and is moving with a
constant speed of 1.8 m s–1.
1.2 m s–1
1.8 m s–1

glider P

The gliders have a perfectly elastic collision.
What are the speeds of the two gliders after the collision?
speed of Q

hints: Take right as positive so glider P has $u_P = +1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and glider Q has $u_Q = -1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, then write total momentum $m_Pu_P+m_Qu_Q$.
For a perfectly elastic collision use both conservation of momentum and conservation of relative speed: approach speed $1.2+1.8 = 3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ equals separation speed.
Solve the two equations $0.30v_P+0.60v_Q = -0.72$ and $v_Q-v_P = 3.0$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ units, then take magnitudes for speeds.
walkthrough: Choose positive to the right. Then $m_P = 0.30\text{ kg}$, $u_P = +1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $m_Q = 0.60\text{ kg}$, $u_Q = -1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from the diagram of gliders moving towards each other.
Conservation of momentum gives $m_Pu_P+m_Qu_Q = m_Pv_P+m_Qv_Q$. Substituting gives $0.30(1.2)+0.60(-1.8) = 0.36-1.08 = -0.72$, so $0.30v_P+0.60v_Q = -0.72$ in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Perfectly elastic also means relative speed is conserved. Approach speed is $1.2-(-1.8) = 3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $v_Q-v_P = 3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute $v_Q = v_P+3.0$ into momentum: $0.30v_P+0.60(v_P+3.0) = -0.72$. This gives $0.90v_P+1.8 = -0.72$, so $0.90v_P = -2.52$ and $v_P = -2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Then $v_Q = -2.8+3.0 = +0.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Speeds are magnitudes, so speed of P is $2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and speed of Q is $0.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Speeds $1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $0.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ do not conserve total kinetic energy, which must stay at $1.188\text{ J}$ for a perfectly elastic collision.

B.explanation: Speeds $2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $1.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ give separation speed $3.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$, not equal to the approach speed $3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ required for elastic collision.

C.explanation: Speeds $2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for P and $0.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for Q conserve both momentum at $-0.72\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ and kinetic energy at $1.188\text{ J}$.

D.explanation: Speeds $3.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $0.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ give too much kinetic energy, about $2.05\text{ J}$, greater than the initial $1.188\text{ J}$.
